description: 100-dps audit of the m_μ prediction residual (210 ppb) post q_0 re-pin (#1422). Localises whether the residual is the propagated q_0 shift (H1: no formula correction needed) or requires a missing structural correction (H2).

parameters.q_canonical_anchor_note: asserted at run time; a muon value here would make the audit difference muon against muon and report the inversion residual as the tension (measured: 0.0747 ppb vs the true 11.61 ppb, 155x understated)

leg_separation.substrate_tension_meaning: proton pin vs muon-anchored q_0 — PHYSICAL (the 9.5σ μ–p disagreement)
leg_separation.inversion_residual_meaning: stored muon literal vs a fresh Newton inversion — SAME pin, two routes; a precision floor, not a physical quantity
leg_separation.why_recorded: the committed witness once reported the residual AS the tension; carrying both makes that substitution visible instead of plausible

data.interpretation: H1 SUPPORTED: the 210 ppb m_μ residual IS the q_0 re-pin shift propagated through Vol(4_1)/ℏ_q². No missing categorical correction to the muon formula. The substrate is fundamentally OVER-DETERMINED — q_0 cannot simultaneously match m_p AND m_μ at sub-ppb precision.

caveats: This file's header says 'Vol(4_1) = 2·Λ(π/3)'. That is wrong by a factor of 3 — 2·Λ(π/3) = Cl₂(2π/3) = 0.6766… = Vol(4_1)/3 — as vol_4_1_mathlib's own docstring already records. The computation uses the correct 2·Cl₂(π/3); only the header is stale. Separately, that helper quotes the SnapPy value as 2.02988321281930725004240510854658…, which is wrong from the 33rd digit; the correct continuation is …5490405718833786150…, as the vol_4_1_matches_known_value assertion records.
